title: Rank-one orientation uniqueness in normalized Stage coordinates
statement: Fix the finite-field and coefficient setting $P$ of [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and finite coefficient subfields of a fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and fix $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$, $p:Z\to Y$ with $j$ open, $p$ proper, and $f=p\circ j$ a $k$-morphism smooth of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Use the actual complete finite-Tor integral categories, completed pullback and tensor, and the specified compact-support/exceptional adjunctions of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Fix $S,M,E,m$ and any Stage $A$ of [def-pur-tower-trace-comparison-data]. For any two arrows $g,h:T_E\to G_E1$ having PrescribedUnitReductions in that same Stage, $g=h$. Neither arrow is required to be invertible.

source.place: Tower-gamma clause (1), rank-one uniqueness, transferred through the fixed adjunction

proof.text: Apply integral orientation reduction injectivity to the shifted Tate line and coefficient unit in the realized model. The normalized source and finite exceptional comparison identify its rho evaluations with the prescribed finite reductions. Cancel these isomorphisms; both evaluation families are the fixed finite unit purity family. Injectivity gives equality of full-subcategory arrows and hence of their underlying maps.
